summary: One router workflow .github/workflows/ci.yaml (name CI) replaces pr-and-main.yaml, envoy-and-contracts.yaml and docs.yaml, and calls worker-image.yaml for pull requests. Triggers: pull_request [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review], push to main, merge_group; no edited, no paths, no schedule. Concurrency per PR ref with cancel on pull_request; per commit and never cancelled on main. A `changes` job (skipped on drafts) runs one dorny/paths-filter step with one filter per job; every test job runs only when its filter is true; lint, typecheck and test keep their ids and a fail-open condition because ruleset 12331919 requires them until the flip; the final job `ci-ok` (if !cancelled()) passes only when changes succeeded and every other job succeeded or skipped, and is red on drafts. Filters name every file each job reads by a reproducible method (go list -deps -test closures, embeds, subprocess targets, runtime reads, step inputs, ci.yaml). No pull-request run writes an Actions cache: worker image layers go to a ghcr registry cache written only from main; Go caches use actions/cache/restore and save only on push; go-notices is keyed on its script and target lists; setup-bun gets no-cache off main. check-image-trigger-paths.sh learns event and draft terms and actions/cache/restore|save; check-bun-version.sh allows no-cache. Cutover: merge under today's ruleset, flip to [ci-ok, pr-title] once every open non-draft non-conflicting PR head carries ci-ok, by session 01a16962 with the admin token.

acceptance.criterion: 1. A title or body edit starts no router run
acceptance.command: gh pr edit <n> --body/--title; gh run list -R sjawhar/legion --workflow ci.yaml --branch <b> shows no new run in 5 min; negative control: a push starts one

acceptance.criterion: 2. Each job's path list names every file it reads
acceptance.surface: ci.yaml filters; local script and scratch PRs
acceptance.command: throwaway script: for each job, the plan 2.4 reference commands (go list -deps -test with tags, embeds, subprocess closures, runtime reads, step inputs) checked against the job's filter with .github/scripts/workflow_paths.py Filter, printing 0 uncovered; negative control: a filter with one dir removed prints the uncovered files; plus one scratch PR per job changing one file of its list, showing the job selected in the changes job outputs

acceptance.criterion: 3. <=5% of test-job minutes in the first 100 PR runs go to unneeded jobs
acceptance.command: production check: script over the first 100 pull_request runs of ci.yaml, job minutes (runner_name non-empty) vs each run's diff against the row-2 reference; pre-merge projection over the last 3 days of PR file lists in the PR body

acceptance.criterion: 4. A draft starts no test job; ready starts them
acceptance.command: gh pr create --draft; jobs API shows only ci-ok with a runner, red with the draft message; gh pr ready <n> starts the selected jobs; negative control: the same change non-draft

acceptance.criterion: 5. 7 days after merge: cache < 9 GB; notices step p90 < 3 min
acceptance.command: production check: gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/actions/cache/usage daily max < 9 GB, no refs/pull/* entry created after the merge; lint notices step durations p90 < 3 min; pre-merge: plan 2.6 projection <= 7 GB and no cache entry for the scratch PRs' refs

acceptance.criterion: 6. A newer push cancels an older head's worker image build
acceptance.surface: scratch PR touching an image input
acceptance.command: push head A, wait for worker-image / build in progress, push head B; A's run and job end cancelled (jobs API); negative control: main release worker builds of two merges both complete

acceptance.criterion: 7. A release run starts within 30 minutes of its merge, 7 days after
acceptance.command: production check: for each push to main touching release.yaml's push paths, the first release.yaml push run at that commit or a descendant created at or after it; min started_at of its jobs with a runner minus the push time <= 30 min

acceptance.criterion: 8. Exact ruleset edit and cutover order in the implement handoff
acceptance.command: the tester compares the handoff's PUT body with a fresh GET of rulesets/12331919: only required_status_checks differs, becoming ci-ok and pr-title with integration_id 15368

acceptance.criterion: 9. The PR states runner minutes and queue time before and after
acceptance.command: before from dispatch://INFRA-490/artifact/ci-router-measurement-2026-10-26-md; after: the projection at merge, the measured first-100-run minutes and queue times in the Production line at the production check
bash .github/scripts/check-image-trigger-paths.test.sh; bash .github/scripts/check-bun-version.test.sh (new tests red on the unmodified checks); both checks pass on the tree
a selected job made to fail, a selected job cancelled, and a failing changes job each turn ci-ok red; with changes failing, lint/typecheck/test still run

decisionsForArchitect: ci.yaml is in every job's filter, so a router edit runs every job; the measurement's reference sets name the workflow file for each job, so those runs count as needed; INFRA-516 chose the opposite for agent-infra (its acceptance 2)
A draft PR's run ends with a red ci-ok and no test job; a Legion PR left a draft would be sent back to its implementer by the daemon's CI-red rule

Acceptance 7 is read as: first release.yaml run covering the merge has a job on a runner within 30 minutes; main pushes stay one group per commit, never cancelled; nothing in this change guarantees the queue time
The release-envoy-listener.yaml gha cache counts in acceptance 5's budget but that file is INFRA-522's change in flight
mergeWaitWarn in packages/daemon/internal/daemon/auto_merge.go stays one hour; only its comment is corrected to the new required set

Between the merge and the ruleset flip, the required set is today's lint, typecheck, test, pr-title; the other router jobs stay advisory until the flip; a stale PR that keeps the flip condition false is the controller's call

findings.finding: B1: cutover by workflow_dispatch on PR branches cannot run (branches have no ci.yaml) and its checks would land at a different SHA; the admin token is directed only for the ruleset edit
findings.answer: workflow_dispatch dropped; cutover is merge under today's ruleset with lint/typecheck/test ids kept, then a flip once every open non-draft non-conflicting PR head carries ci-ok (machine check in plan 2.8), only the ruleset edit uses the admin token; close/reopen ruled out (pr-closed-unmerged)

findings.finding: B1 hidden: kept lint/typecheck/test ids could become passing skips when changes fails under the old ruleset
findings.answer: lint, typecheck and test use a fail-open condition: they run when changes did not succeed (plan 2.3)

findings.finding: B2: the filter method missed files tests read through go subprocesses and repo-root joins, and test's steps
findings.answer: method adds every exec.Command go target's closure and filepath.Abs/repositoryRoot reads; test's filter is the closure plus every file its steps read (plan 2.4)

findings.finding: B3: main-only writes do not bound the cache; worker image buildkit churn, listener gha cache, shared index-buildkit scope, new Go caches, 2.2 GB go-notices per key change
findings.answer: worker image cache moves to a ghcr registry cache written only from main; only jobs that cache today get a Go family; go-notices keyed on its script and target lists; budget projection <= 7 GB with ordered levers; listener coordinated with INFRA-522 (plan 2.6)

findings.finding: B4: release start time not addressed; acceptance 7 ambiguous; queue: max not weighed
findings.answer: acceptance 7 defined as a query (plan row 7); queue: max weighed and rejected with arithmetic (34 merges a day); per-commit main groups kept; noted as a decision for the architect

specDepartures.spec: Pull-request runs read caches and never write them (buildkit cache-to in the Worker Image build, go-notices, setup-go).
specDepartures.plan: The worker image's build cache moves from the Actions cache to a registry cache on ghcr (ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:buildcache), read by every build and written only from main; the setup-bun Bun-binary cache is neither read nor written off main (no-cache), so a PR downloads Bun.
specDepartures.evidence: The Actions cache held 10.80 GB of PR-scope buildkit blobs in 257 entries on 2026-10-27, and main builds the worker image about 16 times a day (measurement section 3), so main-only gha writes would still exceed 9 GB in 7 days; oven-sh/setup-bun has no restore-only mode.
